universities.name: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology
universities.summary: KNUST's School of Medical Sciences was founded in 1975 and runs a direct-entry BSc Human Biology (Medicine) to MB ChB programme, one continuous six-year admission distinct from the university's separate graduate-entry GEMP route. The programme is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG-certification eligibility for graduates from 1982 onward, and clinical training runs at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, the school's teaching hospital since its founding.
universities.campusLifestyle: Admission is decided through a single combined application, entrance exam and interview process covering both the BSc Human Biology (Medicine) and Dentistry tracks, with a formal-dress in-person interview at the School of Medical Sciences in Kumasi. KNUST explicitly warns applicants against using agents or middlemen, stating selection is strictly on merit.
universities.cityProfile: Kumasi is Ghana's second-largest city. The medical school shares a long-standing relationship with Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, which became a dedicated teaching hospital for KNUST's medical programme at the school's founding in 1975.
universities.practicalExposure: The programme runs as one continuous six-year admission: a three-year BSc Human Biology (Medicine) foundation stage covering basic medical sciences with early clinical exposure and community-health orientation, followed directly by a three-year clinical phase based at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital and affiliated sites, without a separate re-application between stages. Graduates receive the MB ChB (Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery) degree.
universities.hostelOverview: International students can book rooms through KNUST's official GUSSS Hostels system, with 2025/26 annual rates ranging from roughly USD 905 (3-in-1 room, 3rd/4th year) to USD 1,255 (2-in-1 room, 1st year), payable in USD to GUSSS Hostels accounts. Short-stay accommodation during the entrance-exam and interview period is also available at GH cedi 20 per bed per night, booked by phone through the exam notice's listed contact.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure is published. Food costs should be planned as part of an independent living-cost budget alongside accommodation.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found. KNUST's admissions communications explicitly warn applicants against dealing with unofficial agents or middlemen during the application process.
universities.studentSupport: International applicants apply through KNUST's central Admissions Portal, with a dedicated international-applicant category and payment channels for USD application fees, including GCB Bank, Ecobank, UBA and the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) for local-currency payment from participating African banks.
whyChoose: Listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools (FAIMER School ID F0000476), currently operational, with ECFMG-certification eligibility for graduates from 1982 onward.

A genuine direct-entry pathway (BSc Human Biology, Medicine) distinct from the university's separate graduate-entry GEMP route, confirmed independently by both KNUST's own admissions notice and the WDOMS record's 'admission follows completion of secondary education' classification.
A 50-year continuous teaching-hospital relationship with Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, one of Ghana's major referral hospitals.
A transparent, published international fee schedule direct from KNUST's own official fee-schedule documents.
A dedicated international-applicant admissions category with multiple payment channels, including a regional payment system (PAPSS) for African-bank customers.
thingsToConsider: KNUST also runs a separate Graduate Entry Medical Programme (GEMP) requiring an already-completed bachelor's degree -- this record covers only the direct-entry BSc Human Biology (Medicine) route, not GEMP.

Ghana's Medical and Dental Council recognition of the programme could not be independently confirmed from a static page (the Council's accredited-institutions list is JavaScript-rendered); this is a data-access limitation, not a specific finding of non-recognition.
The most recent confirmed entrance-exam cycle was held in December 2025 for the 2025/2026 academic year; KNUST had not yet published 2026/27-cycle dates at the time of research.

A Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is referenced by third-party sources as covering Medicine at KNUST, but this could not be independently confirmed on an official KNUST or Mastercard Foundation page, and such schemes typically carry African-nationality or need-based restrictions rather than being open to all international applicants.
Indian applicants must separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission NEET-UG Eligibility Certificate requirement; this is not referenced or administered by the university.
bestFitFor: Students confident preparing for a 100-question multiple-choice entrance exam (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, verbal/quantitative reasoning) plus a formal interview.
Applicants who meet KNUST's WASSCE-equivalent grade thresholds and are comfortable with a merit-based, single-cycle admissions process.
Families able to confirm next-cycle deadlines directly with KNUST given the university has not yet published 2026/27-specific dates.

faq.question: Is the BSc Human Biology (Medicine) to MB ChB programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. It is a single continuous six-year admission -- a three-year Human Biology foundation stage followed directly by a three-year clinical stage -- with no separate bachelor's degree required first. This is different from KNUST's separate Graduate Entry Medical Programme (GEMP), which does require a prior bachelor's degree.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the MB ChB (Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery) degree.

faq.question: What entrance exam does the university require?
faq.answer: A 100-question multiple-choice exam covering Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, and verbal/quantitative reasoning, followed by a formal-dress in-person interview at the School of Medical Sciences in Kumasi.

faq.question: What are the entry-grade requirements?
faq.answer: WASSCE applicants need an aggregate of 8 or better across English, Integrated Science, Core Mathematics, Chemistry, Biology and Physics or Elective Mathematics. A-Level applicants need an aggregate of 08 or better in Biology, Chemistry, Physics and General Paper.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: For 2025/26, international first-year (fresher) students pay a total of USD 7,563, and continuing-year students pay USD 7,097 per year (USD 5,950 tuition plus USD 988.41 in other charges and USD 158.76 in medicine-specific additional charges), per KNUST's official international fee schedule.

faq.question: Are there additional fees besides tuition?
faq.answer: Yes -- a USD 100 application/e-voucher fee and a GH cedi 400 entrance-exam fee for the 2025/26 cycle (this fee is revised each cycle).

faq.question: When does the academic year start and when can I apply?
faq.answer: The most recent confirmed entrance-exam cycle was held in December 2025 for the 2025/2026 academic year. KNUST had not yet published a specific 2026/27-cycle deadline at the time of research -- confirm current dates directly with the School of Medical Sciences.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available for international students?
faq.answer: Yes -- international students can book rooms through KNUST's official GUSSS Hostels system, with 2025/26 annual rates ranging from roughly USD 905 to USD 1,255 depending on room type and year of study.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens and OCI holders who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG, whose result serves as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.

programmes.officialTitle: BSc Human Biology (Medicine) to MB ChB

fee.notes: Officially published 2025/26 international fees: first-year (fresher) total USD 7,563 (combined tuition and charges); continuing years USD 7,097/year, comprising USD 5,950 tuition, USD 988.41 other charges (health care, ICT, registration, library, resident permit, sports) and USD 158.76 medicine-specific additional charges, per KNUST's official fee-schedule PDFs. Total is calculated using the continuing-year rate across 6 years, with the first year's slightly higher USD 7,563 figure -- not published as a single lump sum. A separate USD 100 application/e-voucher fee and a GH cedi 400 entrance-exam fee (revised each cycle) apply. No refund policy was published.

eligibleAudiences: International applicants with WASSCE (aggregate 8+, English/Integrated Science/Core Maths plus Chemistry/Biology/Physics-or-Elective-Maths) or A-Level (aggregate 08+, Biology/Chemistry/Physics/General Paper) or equivalent secondary qualifications
restrictions: Admission is via a 100-question entrance exam plus interview -- no exemption route is offered
Applicants from non-English-speaking countries must provide an English Proficiency Certificate covering at least one year of prior study
Indian applicants must separately hold a current NEET-UG qualification under India's National Medical Commission rules; this is not administered by the university itself
audienceEligibility.notes: This eligibility applies to the direct-entry BSc Human Biology (Medicine) route only, not KNUST's separate graduate-entry GEMP programme, which requires an already-completed bachelor's degree.

admissionsContent.overview: Applicants generate an e-Voucher on KNUST's Admissions Portal, apply as an international candidate, submit academic documents, sit a 100-question entrance exam, and attend a formal in-person interview before a merit-based admission decision.

eligibility.intro: Admission requires a qualifying secondary-education result (WASSCE, A-Level or equivalent), English proficiency, and a passing result on KNUST's own entrance exam and interview.
items: WASSCE aggregate 8+ (English, Integrated Science, Core Maths, Chemistry, Biology, Physics or Elective Maths) or A-Level aggregate 08+ (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, General Paper)
English Proficiency Certificate (at least one year of prior study), for applicants from non-English-speaking countries
100-question multiple-choice entrance exam (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, verbal/quantitative reasoning) plus a formal in-person interview
Indian applicants: current NEET-UG qualification per India's National Medical Commission rules, separate from the university's own admission process

applicationSteps: Generate an e-Voucher via the KNUST Admissions Portal, selecting the International applicant category, and pay the USD 100 application fee
Complete the online application and upload transcripts, certificates and a valid ID

Pay the entrance-exam fee (GH cedi 400 for the 2025/26 cycle) and sit the exam in Kumasi

English Proficiency Certificate, for applicants from non-English-speaking countries
